lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Chatbots and Language AI
lesson.summary: Find out what a chatbot is, how language AI predicts words, when chatbots get it wrong and how to use them safely and honestly.
learning_objectives: Explain that a chatbot is a program and language AI predicts words from patterns
Explain why chatbots can make things up, be out of date or be biased
Use chatbots safely, check answers and write your own work

standards.text: Learning: computers can learn from data, and models make predictions from patterns
Societal impact: AI can impact the world in positive and negative ways

success_criteria: I can say what a chatbot is and that it has no feelings
I can explain that language AI predicts words from patterns
I keep personal information private, check answers and tell a trusted adult
lesson.real_life: A school help chatbot, or a voice helper asked for ideas for a project, with answers checked by a grown-up.

options.text: Something that repeats in a regular way

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how does a chatbot make its words?
blocks.say: Today we meet chatbots. A chatbot can answer in words. But does it understand us?

blocks.alt: A close-up of a red, blue and green macaw parrot against a blurred green background
blocks.caption: A parrot can copy words without knowing their meaning. A chatbot also does not understand like a person.
blocks.credit: Photo by Barbora Dostálová on Unsplash
blocks.say: A parrot can copy words it has heard without knowing what they mean. A chatbot works differently, but it does not think like a person either.

blocks.markdown: A **chatbot** is a program that replies in everyday language.
blocks.say: A chatbot is a computer program that chats in everyday words. People make it, and it runs on a computer.
Some chatbots are scripted. They pick from ready-written replies. Others use AI trained on lots of text.

scenes.caption: Scripted.
scenes.say: The school help bot has a menu. Zara taps opening times and gets a ready-made reply.

scenes.caption: Free typing.
scenes.say: A language AI chatbot lets her type any question in her own words.

scenes.caption: Programs.
scenes.say: Both are programs made by people. Neither one is alive or a person.

question.prompt: Zara taps a menu and gets a ready-made reply about opening times. Which kind of chatbot is this?
question.explanation: A menu with ready-made replies is scripted.

blocks.markdown: A chatbot makes words. It does not have **feelings**.
blocks.say: A chatbot can write I am happy. That does not mean it feels happy. It only makes words.

scenes.caption: A reply.
scenes.say: Zara types: are you sad today? The chatbot writes: I am doing well!

scenes.caption: Patterns.
scenes.say: The reply is built from patterns in text. A program does not feel sad or happy.

scenes.caption: A tool.
scenes.say: So we enjoy using it, but remember what it is: a tool.

question.prompt: If a chatbot writes I am happy, it must feel happy.
question.explanation: A program makes words and has no feelings.

blocks.title: Zara and the school chatbot
blocks.transcript: Zara's class meets a chatbot. It replies in everyday words. A chatbot is a program made by people. It is not alive. It predicts the next word, again and again, using patterns from training text. It names a book about K2. The librarian says the book does not exist. So Zara checks answers in a book. A chatbot can sound sure and be wrong. She never types her address or password. Private things stay private. She writes her K2 poster in her own words. That is her own work. When a reply is unkind, she stops and tells her teacher.
blocks.caption: Zara learns how a chatbot works and how to use it safely.

blocks.text: Stop 1: One word at a time

blocks.markdown: **Training text** is the words the AI learned patterns from.
blocks.say: Language AI learns from huge amounts of text. It finds patterns in which words usually follow other words.

blocks.alt: A long line of white dominoes with black dots standing in a row, fading into a blurred white background
blocks.caption: One word leads to the next, like a chain of dominoes.
blocks.credit: Photo by Robert Stump on Unsplash
blocks.say: When you type, it predicts a likely next word. Then it predicts the next one, like a line of dominoes.

scenes.caption: Start.
scenes.say: The sentence starts: the cat sat on the. What word is likely next?

scenes.caption: Likely.
scenes.say: In its training text, the word mat came next many times. So mat is a likely choice.

scenes.caption: Repeat.
scenes.say: It adds mat, then predicts again. A whole reply is built one word at a time.

question.explanation: Patterns in text make teeth the likely word.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Sounding right is not the same as being right

blocks.markdown: A chatbot can **make things up** that sound true.
blocks.say: A chatbot predicts likely words. Likely words can sound right and still be false.

scenes.caption: Ask.
scenes.say: Zara asks for a book about K2 for children. The chatbot names one.

scenes.caption: Not real.
scenes.say: Zara asks her librarian. That book does not exist. The chatbot made it up.

scenes.caption: Confident.
scenes.say: The chatbot was confident. Being confident does not make an answer true.

question.prompt: A chatbot names a book that no library has. What most likely happened?

blocks.markdown: A chatbot can be **out of date**.
blocks.say: A chatbot learned from old text. It may miss new events, so we cannot trust its news.

blocks.markdown: Text can include **bias**. Play the memory game.
blocks.say: It also learned from text written by people. That text can include unfair ideas, and a chatbot can copy them. First, a memory game.

blocks.say: Zara's class writes rules for using a chatbot. First, always ask a grown-up before you start.
Rule two: never type private things. That means your address, your password and your full name with your school.
Rule three: check important answers in another source. A chatbot can make things up.

scenes.caption: Rule 1.
scenes.say: Rule one is a hand up. Ask a grown-up first.

scenes.caption: Rule 2.
scenes.say: Rule two is a padlock. Personal information stays private.

scenes.caption: Rule 3.
scenes.say: Rule three is a magnifier. Check important answers.

blocks.markdown: Use a chatbot for ideas. Write your own work.
blocks.say: A chatbot can give ideas. Then you must write your own work. Copying is not learning.

blocks.markdown: If it says something unkind, stop and tell a trusted adult.
blocks.say: If a chatbot says something unkind or strange, stop. Tell a trusted adult. It is not your fault.

scenes.caption: Ideas.
scenes.say: Zara asks the chatbot for ideas for her K2 poster. She checks them in a book.

scenes.caption: Own work.

scenes.caption: Tell.
scenes.say: Once, a reply is unkind. She stops and tells her teacher. That is the right thing.
